methods.label: Compare the extra amounts
methods.sourceMethod: Compare the differences in orange and pizza amounts, then recover the whole pizza's weight by fraction division.

annotationRationale: The problem asks for a whole quantity from the weight corresponding to a fractional part. Subtracting unlike fractions and dividing fractions support that task. The supplied balance-equation route uses the same cancellation, so it is not presented as a separate method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The weight is 9/5=1 4/5 pounds, choice A. The current question clearly uses 3 1/2 cups. Random Math's flattened '31/2' is a source-transcription defect; its own equation uses 7/2 correctly. There is no contradiction in the current question, choices, grading, or figures.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The supplied balance-equation solutions perform the same cancellation as the retained comparison method. A separate algebraic version would largely repeat the calculation, so no additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Fraction-division application is appropriately assessed. Unlike-denominator subtraction and fraction division precisely support the written route. Equation-solving nodes are correctly omitted because no unknown-variable equation is set up or solved.
review.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Removing the stated common quantities leaves 3 cups balancing 3/4-1/3=5/12 of a pizza. The cups weigh 3·1/4=3/4 pound. Therefore the whole pizza weighs (3/4)/(5/12)=9/5 pounds. All removals are feasible, and the units and choice A are correct.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both references support comparing the orange and pizza differences. The candidate reconstructs this as a concrete removal argument with original explanatory prose. Source-informed-original correctly reflects the nonofficial sources and does not rely on the Random Math footer as proof of MAA authorship.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The removal operation explains why the remaining weights are equal. The fraction subtraction is shown, and the final division is linked explicitly to recovering the whole from its fractional part. No material transition is omitted.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p184 matches recovering the whole quantity, cnm_p173 matches 3/4-1/3, and cnm_p183 matches division by 5/12 using its reciprocal. All immediate IDs fit their supplied definitions.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All three accepted exact native links match the application and computations. The method demonstrates these particular skills without claiming full coverage of their attached national standards.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 6.NS.A.1 links provide relevant fraction-division coverage. The partial 5.NF.A.1 and 5.NF.A.2 links overlap fraction subtraction and its word-problem use, without covering all mixed-number or estimation requirements. The broader 4.NF.C.5 link concerns tenths and hundredths, which are absent here. The 5.NF.B.7, 5.NF.B.7b, and 5.NF.B.7c links concern restricted unit-fraction cases and do not cover this general quotient. The 7.RP.A.1 link offers only partial unit-quantity overlap.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The assessed application and two supporting procedures are precise. The incidental integer-times-fraction calculation does not require an additional direct node.
